one_liner: Tiny ISC-licensed C streaming (SAX) JSON parser and generator; its DOM layer parsed 1.3x faster than json-c in nativejson-benchmark.
what_it_does: YAJL is an event-driven JSON parser and generator in C99. You allocate a handle with a table of callbacks (null, boolean, integer, double or raw number, string, map start/key/end, array start/end), then feed bytes with yajl_parse() as often as you like and finish with yajl_complete_parse(); a token split across chunks is buffered internally. yajl_tree_parse() is a convenience layer that builds a simple yajl_val tree from a NUL-terminated string, and yajl_gen writes JSON. It is not API-compatible with json-c, Jansson or JsonCpp.
how_it_is_fast: A hand-written byte-at-a-time lexer classifies characters through a 256-entry lookup table, and yajl_string_scan skips runs of ordinary string bytes in a tight loop (the 2.0 'string scanning' tweak the ChangeLog credits with a 20-35% speedup). Strings without escapes are handed to callbacks as pointers into the caller's buffer (zero copy); escaped strings are decoded into one reusable buffer, and nesting is tracked with an explicit byte stack instead of recursion. There is no SIMD; the DOM-parse win over json-c in the benchmark comes mostly from canada.json, and the tree is lighter (12.9 MB vs 33.7 MB for json-c on that file).
when_to_use: JSON that arrives in chunks (sockets, pipes, block reads) where you want callbacks as tokens complete instead of buffering the whole document.
Streams of concatenated or whitespace-separated JSON values (yajl_allow_multiple_values), or filters and reformatters that never build a tree, like the bundled json_reformat and json_verify.
Validation where a human-readable error with surrounding input text and a position arrow matters (yajl_get_error with verbose set).
C code bound by json-c 0.12 or JsonCpp 1.0 DOM parsing on number-heavy documents that wants about 1.3-1.6x and a smaller tree, and can take a different API.
Systems already linked against a distribution yajl package (Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora shipped patches for the three CVEs in July 2023), where switching libraries costs more than the speed gap.
when_not_to_use: Untrusted input on unpatched upstream code: CVE-2017-16516 (escape-sequence decoding bounds), CVE-2022-24795 (heap corruption with ~2 GB inputs in yajl_buf) and CVE-2023-33460 (yajl_tree_parse leak on error) are open upstream, and issue #260 (2026-08-03) shows an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read in hexToDigit at HEAD.

Throughput-critical DOM parsing: in the same run RapidJSON took 7.93 ms vs YAJL's 103.45 ms over the three files (13x) and cJSON 24.67 ms (about 4.2x, derived from page data); simdjson and yyjson are faster still.

Serialization: stringify was 2.5x slower than json-c (78.64 vs 30.80 ms), yajl_gen prints doubles with sprintf %.20g so [1.2345] does not round-trip (conformance roundtrip22/23 fail), and strtod/sprintf follow the C locale's decimal separator (open issues #79 and #222).

Large or deep trees through yajl_tree: it reallocs object and array storage on every added element, mallocs a copy of every string and number text, runs an integer parse plus strtod per number, looks keys up linearly in yajl_tree_get and frees recursively; its own header pitches it for 'smallish JSON docs'.

Exact numeric and string edge cases: INT64_MIN is rejected as 'integer overflow' through the integer callback, subnormal and underflowing doubles lose YAJL_NUMBER_DOUBLE_VALID in the tree, and tree strings have no length so an embedded \u0000 truncates them (57/66 double and 8/9 string conformance).

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (CMake builds yajl_s and yajl); small enough to source-drop (about 2,700 lines in src/*.c) if you supply the CMake-generated yajl_version.h and a yajl/ include directory
integration.dependencies: none beyond the C library (strtod, sprintf, malloc)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 compiler (required since 2.0.0); CMake 2.6+ for the bundled build
integration.platforms: any: portable C with no intrinsics; ChangeLog and CMakeLists cover Linux, macOS, Windows (MSVC/nmake), NetBSD and QNX
integration.thread_safety: not documented; from the source all parser state lives in the handle and the character table is const, so one handle per thread works, but number conversion depends on the process-wide C locale

gotchas: Unpaired high surrogate bug (from source reading): yajl_string_decode emits '?' for a \uD800-\uDBFF escape not followed by \u, then also skips the next input byte, so "\ud83dabc" decodes to "?bc"; when the skipped byte is the first half of an escaped backslash, the second backslash is taken as an escape start and hexToDigit reads 4 bytes past the token, which is exactly issue #260's reproducer ["e2d\ud83d\\u0"]. A high surrogate followed by any \u escape is combined without checking for a low surrogate, and UTF-8 validation only checks lead and continuation bit patterns (overlong and surrogate encodings pass).

yajl_tree_parse silently turns on comment support, measures input with strlen (NUL-terminated only), leaks the partial tree on a parse error (CVE-2023-33460, issues #55, #102, #113, #223, #250 all open) and never checks yajl_alloc for NULL; the lexer also accepts \v and \f as whitespace.

No malloc failure checks in yajl_alloc, yajl_lex_alloc or yajl_buf (issue #6 open since 2009); the parser has no nesting limit while yajl_tree_free recurses, and yajl_gen has a compile-time depth limit of YAJL_MAX_DEPTH 128 that a caller cannot raise by redefining the macro in its own translation unit.

Benchmark harness notes (nativejson-benchmark src/tests/yajltest.cpp at a4a9f10), none affecting the timed DOM-parse rows: Parse is best of 10 with the tree freed outside the timer for every library; the Stringify fallback for numbers that are neither int- nor double-valid calls strlen(buffer) on an uninitialized stack array instead of strlen(num) (not reached on the three files, which pass Verify); SaxRoundtrip calls yajl_gen_clear before returning, so its result string is empty, but that output is never checked and the timed work is complete. The 9 double conformance failures (double19, 21-23, 26, 32-34, 37) are all inputs whose value is subnormal or underflows: yajl_tree drops the double-valid flag whenever strtod sets ERANGE.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick YAJL over json-c, Jansson or cJSON only when you need a push-style SAX parser in C that takes input in arbitrary chunks and multiple concatenated values with verbose error context, and you can carry the distribution CVE patches; for building a DOM, cJSON (about 4.2x faster in the same run), yyjson or simdjson are better, and json-c is faster at stringify.
verified_claims_summary: In nativejson-benchmark's 2016-09-09 sample (Core i7-4980HQ, Apple clang 7.0 64-bit, premake optimize Full with -march=native, best of 10 runs), YAJL at commit 5e3a785 building a yajl_tree DOM took 103.45 ms summed over canada, citm_catalog and twitter vs json-c 0.12.1 at 134.55 ms (1.30x), JsonCpp 1.0.0 at 165.52 ms (1.60x) and Jansson 2.7 at 112.06 ms (1.08x); the margin comes from canada.json (75.62 vs 105.78 ms), YAJL is slower than json-c on twitter.json (8.28 vs 7.65 ms), and its tree traversal took 1.07 vs 2.99 ms. The project itself publishes no comparison: the in-tree perf/perftest.c times validation-only parsing with no callbacks, and the README's hope to match the fastest parser is not borne out (RapidJSON 7.93 ms).
status_note: Abandoned: the last commit is 2015-09-24 (5e3a785, the same commit the benchmark measured, so the numbers describe current code), with 89 open issues, 79 open PRs, an unanswered 2025 repository-transfer request (#258) and three CVEs unfixed upstream; ISC-licensed and small enough to vendor, but take the Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora patches and fix the surrogate-skip bug before parsing untrusted input.
